summary: Taion Satomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University until 1933. He later served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College, attested in 1972.

Taira Shidehara specialized in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1891 to 1894, later holding posts there (~1900–1906) and at Tokyo University of Education (~1906–1919).
Tairyu Tsunoda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Taisen Deshimaru worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under teacher Kodo Sawaki from circa 1936 to 1965. He founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1978–2006) and as a concurrent lecturer at the Eastern Institute (attested 1990).

Taishun Mibu specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After completing his studies at Taisho University in 1937, he taught Ryosho Onami and served as director at Taisho University, attested in 1972.

Taitetsu Unno worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, he taught Jeff Wilson and Leo M. Pruden and served as a professor of religion at Smith College (1971–1998).

Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1950–1954) and under traditional teacher Mumon Yamada (~1954–1988). He later held a post at Hanazono University from circa 1996 to 2002.

Taixu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jingan, Jichan, and Yang Renshan. He led the Minnan Buddhist Academy in 1927 and founded several institutions, including the Wuchang Buddhist Institute and the World Buddhist Federation.

Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, SFSU, and under teachers Hakujun Kuroda, Hakuun Yasutani, and Koryu Osaka. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission and founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Sze earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen.

Taka Yanagisawa worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Japan Women's University, she served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties and taught Anne Nishimura Morse.

Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2015, Kameyama held positions as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Buddhist studies scholar Takamaro Shigaraki earned a PhD from Ryukoku University, later serving as professor and president (1989–1995). He also studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and IBS, and served as chairman of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. He taught Kangei Okamoto and held multiple posts at Waseda University, serving as professor from 1915 and Dean of the Faculty of Letters in 1930.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Taisho University and Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, later mentored by Heinz Bechert. Fukita was attested as a lecturer at Bukkyo University in 1999.

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University. He held faculty posts at International Buddhist University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996–2016).
Takanori Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996) and as head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).

Takanori Shintani is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977) and held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1994–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010–2019).
